semantic_repairs: Timer arm, stored logical deadline, scheduler callback, protocol action, and state termination are distinct events and timestamps.
Mathematical formulas use standard G; executable MightyPPL formulas use weak finite-word G* under an explicitly closed one-generation projection.
Every bounded eventual property has an early counterexample and a negative_late_or_missing counterexample; every legal supersession has a positive trace.
Every admitted AP is assigned to at least one fixed primary or auxiliary source mapping; mappings carry only their source-specific AP subsets.
Every re-arm/reset creates a new timer_generation and a fresh monitor; overlapping trigger generations are excluded from one finite word.

screened_documents.use: Timer A--K, Timer C strict bound, transaction state and supersession rules
Accepted states, Timer D/L/M, UAS-core 2xx retransmission schedule

fixed_implementations.property_scope: SIP-TX-20 Timer C initial/reset generation and lifetime interaction

known_deviation_profiles.finding: fr_inv_timeout defaults to 120000 ms and max_inv_lifetime to exactly 180000 ms, while RFC 3261 requires Timer C strictly greater than 180000 ms.
known_deviation_profiles.catalog_treatment: NORMATIVE strict-bound oracle; fixed default profile is EXPECTED_VIOLATION unless configuration is pinned above the bound.

known_deviation_profiles.finding: The initial handler shifts 500 to 1000 after scheduling; the first callback shifts again before scheduling, producing a 2000-ms next interval rather than 1000 ms.
known_deviation_profiles.catalog_treatment: NORMATIVE_EXPECTED_VIOLATION_PROFILE with an explicit source-realistic negative trace.

known_deviation_profiles.finding: Timer X uses timeout <<= 1 without min(...,T2), permitting 8000-ms and longer intervals.
known_deviation_profiles.catalog_treatment: One fresh 4000-ms monitor per post-cap generation; 8000-ms source behavior is an explicit negative trace.

known_deviation_profiles.finding: The FSM registers Any transport error -> Terminated although the RFC 6026 server-side retention property has no such early-discard exception.
known_deviation_profiles.catalog_treatment: All termination paths must emit the AP; the early transport path is an explicit known-deviation negative.

deduplication.reason: The RFC gives a causal callback action but no non-punctual callback/send latency bound measured from the earlier arm; the timing obligations duplicate TX-01/TX-07/TX-13.
